findings.problem: This is the key step of the whole method, but the board jumps from 2^{2x} to (2^x)^2. The only reason given is "two X is double X" and a note "Times power, used backwards", so a student cannot see which number plays m and which plays n.
findings.fix: Write the middle step on the line, 2^{2x} = 2^{x×2} = (2^x)^2. Say "two X is X times two, so by times power this is two to the X, all squared", and change the note to (a^m)^n = a^{mn} with m = x, n = 2.

findings.problem: The voice works out "two times X", but the board goes straight from (2^2)^x to 2^{2x}, so the multiplication the voice describes is never seen.
findings.fix: Write (2^2)^x = 2^{2×x} = 2^{2x} on the words "multiply the powers, two times X".

findings.problem: The voice says to write four with base two because the other term is 2^x, but never says why matching bases helps: it lets both terms be written using 2^x, so one letter can stand for it.
findings.fix: Add one short sentence, e.g. "With the same base, both terms can be written using two to the power X".

findings.problem: "A quadratic in disguise" is said but not explained or shown. A student may not see that one term is the square of the other, just as a² and a are in a quadratic.
findings.fix: Say "one term is the square of the other, like A squared and A", and write a short note under the lit terms, e.g. (2^x)^2 and 2^x ↔ a^2 and a.

findings.problem: This beat must make sense on its own, but it gives no reason why 1 is 2^0 or why x = 0 follows. Beat 17 gave the "powers are equal" reason only for the first value.
findings.fix: Add "any number to the power zero is one" and "both sides have base two, so the powers are equal", lighting line 10 as it is said.
